source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Vesicant extravasation usually causes only transient skin discoloration without deeper tissue injury.","B":"Burning at the site confirms a systemic allergic reaction rather than a local infusion complication.","C":"Tissue injury is unlikely once the IV catheter is in a peripheral vein, so the infusion can continue while the site is observed.","D":"Extravasation of a vesicant can cause severe local tissue injury, including necrosis, and requires prompt management."}}
source_row.rationale: Vesicant extravasation can produce pain, swelling and serious local injury, including tissue necrosis. Prompt recognition and management are needed to limit damage.

source_row.stem: During infusion of a vesicant antineoplastic drug, the client reports burning and swelling at the IV site. Why is this finding urgent?
